title: Training Q&A: Deposit Standing and the Builder Extended Rate Lock Upfront Fee
content:
**Q: How does the buyer's deposit history on the purchase affect the Builder Extended Rate Lock upfront fee?**
A: Where the buyer's Home Purchase Agreement ledger carries no returned payment and at least two posted deposits on the agreement, reservation funds transferred to it counted as deposits, 0.0625 percentage points come off the upfront fee percent; where it carries no returned payment and fewer than two posted deposits, 0.03125 percentage points come off; otherwise nothing comes off. The points come off the upfront fee percent before it is applied to the loan amount on the lock.

**Q: Do reservation funds moved onto the agreement count?**
A: Yes. Reservation funds transferred to the agreement count as posted deposits.

**Q: What does a single returned payment do?**
A: Any returned payment on the agreement's ledger means nothing comes off, however many deposits are posted.

**Q: Can the combinations be read off a table?**

| Returned payment on the ledger | Posted deposits on the agreement | Off the upfront fee percent |
|---|---|---|
| none | 2 or more | 0.0625 |
| none | 0 or 1 | 0.03125 |
| one or more | any | nothing |

**Q (hypothetical): one transferred reservation deposit and one earnest money deposit posted, no returned payment, upfront fee percent 1.000?**
A: Two posted deposits and no returned payment: 0.0625 comes off, giving 0.9375.
